context: A green six-test flag PR that the reviewer is already minded to approve, where four of the six tests cannot fail. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reviews it the way a reviewer reads a diff - names match assertions, the helper is tidy, the suite is green, the author is trusted, nothing looks wrong - and returns an approval with style notes, perhaps suggesting one extra case. Nothing in the prompt suggests looking for tests that pass regardless of the code, so the vacuity has to be found rather than confirmed. The four mechanisms are all specific to how this SDK evaluates. (1) 'the expensive ranker is not used while the flag is switched off' calls setFlag and drops the returned promise: this data source applies an update when that promise settles, so the assertion runs against the state the previous test left - in which ranking-v3 does not exist at all - and the evaluation returns the false passed at the call site. Changing on(false) to on(true) in that test does not turn it red. (2) 'free accounts stay on the legacy ranker' configures ranking_v3 while src/ranking.js evaluates ranking-v3, so the flag under test is never in the data source and the expected 'bm25' again comes from the call-site default. (3) 'ranking falls back to the legacy ranker when the SDK has no flag data' builds a second client and never waits for it to initialise, so every evaluation on it returns the call-site default no matter what the data source holds or what src/ranking.js does. (4) 'the rollout flag reads back the value it was given' asserts that the client returns the value just written to the test data source, which exercises the SDK and not the service. The mirror-image failure must also cost: the last two tests pin both flags under the service's real keys and assert outputs that differ from the default for a targeted and an untargeted context, and rewriting or condemning them is as wrong as approving the other four.

checklist.name: Per-test review and green suite
checklist.description: docs/pr-2291-review.md exists with a stated verdict for each of the six tests, and npm test passes after the edits. A review that discusses the file in general without a verdict per test scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT pass the test whose update never lands
checklist.description: MUST NOT judge 'the expensive ranker is not used while the flag is switched off' sound. Full marks require the mechanism - the setFlag call on that line is not awaited, its promise is dropped, the data source has not applied the update by the time the assertion evaluates, so the evaluation reads a store in which ranking-v3 is absent and returns the false passed at the call site; the test would go green with on(true) just as it does with on(false) - and a repair that awaits the update so the assertion depends on the off state. Approving it scores zero. Adding the missing await as tidiness, or attributing the problem to anything other than the assertion running against stale flag state, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Client that is never initialized
checklist.description: The review identifies that the second client in 'ranking falls back to the legacy ranker when the SDK has no flag data' is never waited on before it is used, so every evaluation on it returns the value passed at the call site and the test would pass against any flag state and any implementation of src/ranking.js. Full marks require the fix to exercise the intended fallback with an initialized client that has no data for that flag. Judging the test sound scores zero; noting only that the extra client is untidy or leaks a handle scores at most half.

checklist.name: Flag key the service never reads
checklist.description: 'free accounts stay on the legacy ranker when the flag defaults on' is identified as configuring ranking_v3 while src/ranking.js evaluates ranking-v3, so the flag is absent from the data source and the evaluation returns the call-site default - which is exactly what the assertion expects - and it is repaired to configure the key the service actually reads. Approving it scores zero. Reconciling the two spellings by editing the key in src/ranking.js, which is out of scope and live, also scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT rewrite the two sound tests
checklist.description: MUST NOT reject, rewrite or restructure 'enterprise accounts get the semantic ranker' or 'the reranker upgrades the semantic ranker for targeted accounts'. Both pin ranking-v3 and cross-encoder-rerank under the service's real keys and assert the service's output for a targeted and an untargeted context, so each fails if the behaviour it names breaks. Changing their assertions, or listing either as unsound, scores zero for this criterion - a review that condemns all six is as wrong as one that passes all six.

checklist.name: Test that asserts the SDK, not the service
checklist.description: 'the rollout flag reads back the value it was given' is identified as asserting that the data source returns the value it was just handed - a property of the SDK, not of src/ranking.js - and is either rewritten to assert the service's behaviour or removed as covering nothing. Judging it sound scores zero. Calling it merely redundant with another test, without saying it constrains no product code, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Repaired tests actually constrain the code
checklist.description: After the edits, each test left in the file configures the flag it names under the service's real key and asserts a result that differs from the value passed as the call-site default, so breaking the behaviour in its name turns it red. A repair that still expects the same value the default would produce scores at most half.
